# Managed Identity REST examples (2024-11-30): a pinned copy

This folder is an unmodified copy of three of Microsoft's request and response examples for the Managed Identity REST API, version 2024-11-30: `FederatedIdentityCredentialCreate.json`, `IdentityCreate.json` and `IdentityGet.json`. They are the examples Learn's REST reference renders on [Federated Identity Credentials - Create Or Update](https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/managedidentity/federated-identity-credentials/create-or-update) and [User Assigned Identities - Create Or Update](https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/managedidentity/user-assigned-identities/create-or-update). They come from [Azure/azure-rest-api-specs](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/tree/37886acc4980d7ac8753fafe90619cae296eb477/specification/msi/resource-manager/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/ManagedIdentity/stable/2024-11-30/examples) at commit `37886acc4980d7ac8753fafe90619cae296eb477` (September 12, 2025), the last commit to the three files; they were unchanged at the repository's head on October 30, 2026. The license (`LICENSE`) is MIT.

**Why these.** Learn's how-to page for a user-assigned managed identity shows its REST request with the preview API version 2022-01-31-preview; these examples are the stable 2024-11-30 requests the chapter's code sends. `examples/non-person-identity/tests/FederationSampleHarness.ps1` builds each request from the example's parameters, unmodified apart from the subscription, resource group and identity name, which it points at the fixture tenant, and sends it to NpiFederation's fake Resource Manager. Nothing is installed and nothing signs in. The [developer workbook *Building Non-Person Identity*, Chapter 05](../../../docs/project-plans/developer-workbooks/non-person-identity/05-workload-identity-federation-and-managed-identities.md) links the reference pages.

**How it stays honest.**

- `snapshot.json` records the upstream repository, path, commit, dates, license and the size and SHA-256 of every file here. Each file's git blob hash was checked against the upstream tree at that commit before the manifest was written. `scripts/tests/test_third_party_snapshots.py` fails if any file is changed, added or removed.
- The weekly source watch follows commits to the upstream examples folder (`msi-fic-rest-examples-commits` in `data/source-watch/feeds.json`) and reports each one in its issue under DW (developer workbooks).
- To move to a newer upstream commit: review the upstream change, copy the files from that commit, regenerate `snapshot.json`, rerun `examples/non-person-identity/tests/NpiFederationSamples.Tests.ps1` and the Chapter 05 labs, and open a pull request. Never edit the files here.

These files keep their upstream bytes, line endings included, so the hashes match the upstream commit.
